extracted.intended_audience: researchers (authors and reviewers) in the life sciences considering eLife submissions
extracted.subtask_description: High-level editorial and peer-review standards and operational principles used by the journal eLife, describing what kinds of papers they aim to publish and how peer review is conducted. Intended to guide authors on expectations and reviewers/editors on process norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired qualities of published papers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our goal at eLife is to publish papers that our reviewers and editors find authoritative, rigorous, insightful, enlightening or just beautiful."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the high-level evaluative attributes editors and reviewers should look for when selecting and assessing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article types and format allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife publishes Research Articles (with no limits to the length or number of figures), Short Reports, Tools and Resources, and Research Advances, plus Magazine content (Editorials, Feature Articles, Insights, podcasts, interviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For details and requirements for each type of submission (formatting, scope, etc.), consult the Author Guide and Policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult Author Guide for submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For details and requirements for each type of submission, please consult our Author Guide and Policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural and format-specific criteria (e.g., what qualifies as a Research Advance versus a Short Report) are specified in the Author Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection by working scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife relies on the judgment of the working scientists who serve as our editors to select papers for peer review and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions are made by active researchers rather than purely professional editors; this principle underpins selection and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial limits on publication volume or acceptance rate
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not artificially limit the number of articles we publish or have a set acceptance rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is driven by quality as judged by editors and reviewers rather than quota-driven acceptance/decline targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife does not use the Impact Factor
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife does not support the Impact Factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal rejects Impact Factor as a guiding metric for editorial decisions or assessment of papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive and collaborative peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Our goal is to make peer review constructive and collaborative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review should aim to improve manuscripts and engage authors and reviewers in a cooperative process rather than adversarial critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid initial decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is an explicit procedural priority in the review workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated revision requests following internal consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision requests are consolidated following an open, internal consultation among reviewers to deliver a single, concise set of the essential revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than multiple, possibly conflicting lists from individual reviewers, the reviewers consult internally so authors receive one prioritized, concise set of required revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of post-review decisions and author responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-review decisions and author responses for published papers are available for all to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife publishes review history information to promote openness about editorial decisions and the revision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of editorial process metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly updated metrics relating to the eLife editorial process are available in our Author Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational metrics (e.g., times to decision) are tracked and made available to inform authors about the journal's performance.
